correctness.rationale: For each all positive integer degrees and horizons, exact radial disk moments show a positive invertible bilateral weighted shift. The product of any N consecutive weights is explicitly telescoped. A crossing path has squared inverse coefficient the crossing inverse-product function, whose log second derivative is at least two positive reciprocal-square terms; its endpoints reduce all paths to a balanced quadratic in the crossing length, maximized only at balanced integer indices. Disjoint output basis directions characterize the complete norming subspace. Compact perturbation and spectral-radius estimates give the circle spectrum. Independently enumerated exact-rational finite cases support, but are not used in place of, this argument.

value.rationale: Finite-horizon inverse amplification is a quantitative operator-dynamical invariant not determined by the spectral circle or forward power bound. Here the canonical harmonic Bergman monomial operators exhibit exact linear growth with slope half the monomial degree, and the norming Fourier modes have a sharp one/two-dimensional parity law. The strict crossing-residue optimization is structural and works for every symbol degree and horizon, furnishing a reproducible benchmark for reversible yet asymmetrically power-bounded Toeplitz operators. No arbitrary cutoff, renaming, or unmotivated numerical slice.
